per_driver_behaviour.driver: ATI Radeon HD 3850 AGP, Catalyst 8.970.100.0 (13.4 legacy, ati2mtag.sys + ati2dvag.dll). This is the same build as /mnt/retro-share/Files/Drivers/ATI/WinXP/Radeon/Catalyst134-Legacy-XP-Display (DriverVer 8.970.100.0000). Monitor: DELL P2312H analog LCD, EDID vmax 76. Persisted desktop 1920x1080x32@60.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: INFERRED, NOT MEASURED. The OS picks the rate, not the game. For a request with no rate, XP's win32k chooses the adapter's default for that mode, which is 60 Hz wherever 60 is listed. Sources: (1) Microsoft's IDirectDraw7::SetDisplayMode doc: 'Set this value to 0 to request the default refresh rate for the driver'. (2) PST/E-Prime KB 17198, from a search-result excerpt because the page itself returned 403: 'On Windows 2000/XP systems ... the display adapter's default refresh rate, which is typically 60hz'. (3) Our only XP measurement, in agent/tools/refreshlogic.h: on .124 with a GeForce2 GTS and ForceWare 71.89 (2026-08-25), the desktop was at 1024x768@100, Quake II went fullscreen at 1024x768, and DISPLAYCFG read 60. At the native 1920x1080 this costs nothing, because 60 is the only listed rate. At the 4:3 fallback 1280x960 (the Q2/SiN/SoF/Q1/WON Half-Life target), GAMERES at 00:26 lists 75, so a title that names no rate should get 60 there instead of 75. The modetest plan's step 1 (test A) measures this.
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: UNMEASURED on ATI. Evidence against it on XP: the PST KB says 'the default refresh rate is used even if the experiment and desktop settings match', and on ForceWare 71.89 the rate went 100 -> 60 at the same 1024x768. One thing could change the ATI answer: both ATI miniports contain the string DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE, a DAL rule that is undocumented and absent from this device key (so unset). The modetest plan's step 1 (test B: set 1280x960@75, then send the no-rate request) answers it. On the native 1080p mode the question is moot, since only 60 exists.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: No working override was found. 3D_Refresh_Rate_Override_DEF=0 exists in the device key {0D44A787-...}\0000 (read 00:34), and CX156444.inf sets it in every chip section. However, none of the 8 binaries in the package reads a 3D_Refresh_Rate_Override value in ASCII or UTF-16: ati2mtag.sys, ati2dvag.dll, ati3duag.dll, atioglxx.dll, ati2evxx.exe, ati2edxx.dll, atiadlxx.dll and ati2cqag.dll were checked (evidence-refresh/mechanism/driver-strings/ati-catalyst134.txt). The setting is vestigial. The only candidates left: (1) DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE, which is undocumented, is read at driver init so needs a reboot, and is a driver-setting change. (2) The OS-level DirectDraw ForceRefreshRate, which is a single rate for every mode and so wrong at 60-only 1080p. (3) Pinning the monitor's MODES ranges. The desktop is already at its best rate, 1920x1080@60.

per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: 60 Hz. It is the only rate the driver lists at every one of its 20 modes (GAMERES 00:26: every entry @60). WDDM's own rule for a no-rate request was not measured and does not matter here: whatever it picks is 60, which is already the best.

per_driver_behaviour.driver: GDI/DirectDraw: Cirrus Logic 5436 PCI (cirrusmm.drv, mini-VDD cirrus.vxd, dated 4-23-1999), DirectX 6.1, no d3d9. 3D: a Voodoo 2 pass-through running the 3.02.02 kit (GLIDE2X.DLL = Glide 2.56, GLIDE3X.DLL = 3.03). Monitor: the roster names a DELL E773c CRT; no EDID is read. Persisted 1024x768x8 @75.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: INFERRED 75 Hz at every mode the Cirrus can scan at 75. Win9x has no per-mode rate for a no-rate request: the display driver applies the display class's single RefreshRate string, HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Class\Display\0000\DEFAULT RefreshRate="75" (read 00:40), to every mode. EnumDisplaySettings lists every mode at 0 Hz, and the live mode reads refresh 0 with registry_refresh 75 (DISPLAYCFG 00:40). UNMEASURED, and on Win9x only timing the scanout can measure it; modetest's -list and steps 1-2 do that with WaitForVerticalBlank. The Voodoo 2 is a separate path. It scans out at the rate the app passes to grSstWinOpen (usually 60) unless SSTV2_SCREENREFRESH (75/85/120, anything else = 60) or SSTV2_REFRESH_<W>x<H> is set. Glide reads these from the process environment first, then HKLM\Software\3Dfx Interactive\Voodoo2\Glide, then ...\Voodoo2, then voodoo2.ini: see glide2x/cvg/init/parse.c:1094 sst1InitGetenv and video.c:1062/1144 sst1InitFindVideoTimingStruct. The fleet kit's binaries carry these names (driver-strings/glide-refresh-strings.txt). On .243 the Glide key holds only SSTV2_R/G/BGAMMA=1.30 (read 00:41), so no refresh override is set.
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: YES by design, inferred: a single global setting governs every mode. Glide keeps nothing between opens; each grSstWinOpen programs its own timing.
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: The RefreshRate string itself is the Win9x override, and it is already 75. 'Optimal' (-1) needs a monitor INF or EDID this box does not have. For the Voodoo 2, a per-launch environment variable such as SSTV2_REFRESH_800x600=<hz> works: the process environment wins over the registry, and it is not a driver change. With no EDID it needs a ceiling that an operator declares. The E773c spec I recall is about 30-70 kHz / 50-160 Hz; this is UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed on the monitor. Writing the same value to HKLM\...\Voodoo2\Glide would be a 3dfx driver setting, so it is never done automatically.

per_driver_behaviour.box: .124 (NSC-C543575F526), Windows XP SP3. NOT touched: it belongs to the V5 6000 lane.
per_driver_behaviour.driver: vcr-kmd 0.1.0.0 (OUR vcrmp.sys + vcrdd.dll, dated 9-25-2026) on the Voodoo 5 6000. Glide is our h5 glide3x or AmigaMerlin's; the ICD is our MesaFX (0.1.64+ has fxBestRefresh). Monitor: HP P1120 21" CRT, EDID native 1600x1200@85, vmax 160. Persisted 1280x1024x32@85.
per_driver_behaviour.no_freq_mode_change_lands_on: XP decides, not vcr-kmd (see vcrkmd_notes). win32k resolves the partial DEVMODE against vcrdd's DrvGetModes list and hands DrvEnablePDEV one listed rate, which vcrdd programs exactly. UNMEASURED which rate win32k picks. The ForceWare result points to the lowest or first-listed (60 for most sizes). vcr-kmd lists 1152x864 with 75 FIRST, so the plan's step 2 on that mode separates the lowest (60), the first-listed (75) and a carried-over rate (85). So GDI/DDraw/D3D titles probably get 60 where 85 is listed. Glide titles do not take this path. MesaFX's fxBestRefresh (fxapi.c:406) asks for the highest enumerated rate at W x H (85). Then our h5 Glide's hwcInitVideo (minihwc.c:4675) replaces it with FX_GLIDE_REFRESH, read through hwcGetenv (process env, then HKCU, then HKLM regPath; minihwc.c:9547). On this box that value comes from the leftover AmigaMerlin key Services\3dfxvs\Device0\glide FX_GLIDE_REFRESH="75" (read 00:38; retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md:422 records that our Glide reads that key). So Glide titles run at 75 where 75 is listed, and at XP's default where it is not (win_mode.c:331/352 retries with rate 0).
per_driver_behaviour.same_res_keeps_current_rate: UNMEASURED. vcr-kmd neither keeps nor chooses a rate; it programs whatever win32k hands it. The plan's steps 1-2 answer this. Alternatively, read the vcr-kmd flight recorder after a game starts: every DrvEnablePDEV logs its w/h/bpp/freq (display/vcrdd.c:425, VCR_EV_DD_ENABLE_PDEV). The historical ring captures in evidence/silicon hold only boot/install mode sets (1280x1024x32@85).
per_driver_behaviour.driver_override_available: vcr-kmd has none by design; Diag\EdidFilter and MonTrustEnvelope only shape the mode list. For Glide there are two per-launch routes: the FX_GLIDE_REFRESH environment variable (it beats the registry in hwcGetenv) or MesaFX's FX_GLIDE_REFRESH_RATE. The registry value FX_GLIDE_REFRESH=75 is a 3dfx driver setting and must not be changed automatically; it is the V5 lane's decision, and changing the effective refresh also changes benchmark comparability (docs/v56k-benchmark-plan.md pins refresh). Observed limit: vcr-kmd lists nothing above 85 Hz (GAMERES 00:26), even though the EDID says vmax 160 and vcr_timings has 100/120 Hz rows. This is an open question.

vcrkmd_notes:
vcr-kmd never sees a no-rate request from an application. On XP, win32k resolves the refresh before the driver is called, and vcr-kmd then honours exactly the rate it is handed. Cited against voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd at origin/master e02dc77:
1) The miniport's mode set comes from common/vcr_modes.c vcr_timings[] (line 18), which has SEVERAL rates per size. Examples: 1024x768 at 60/70/75/85 in the DMT block plus 100 in the vendor-decoded block; 1152x864 at 75 in the DMT row (line 41), then 60/70/85/100 (from line 84); 1280x960 at 60/85 then 75. Each (timing, depth 8/16/32) is kept only if vcr_mode_check (line 162) passes: RAMDAC dot clock, CRTC field range, memory, and the monitor's H/V/dot-clock range. That range comes from vcr_mon_select in include/vcr_edid.h: the EDID read over DDC this boot; else a range persisted by the same monitor; else the envelope intersected with the conservative default (H 30-48 kHz / V 50-75 Hz / 80 MHz); else that default. vcr_modes_build (line 362) keeps table order. miniport/vcrmp.c mode_info sets VIDEO_MODE_INFORMATION.Frequency = t->refresh, the nominal Hz (line 352). IOCTL_VIDEO_QUERY_AVAIL_MODES is at line 650.
2) display/vcrdd.c DrvGetModes (line 206) reports EVERY listed (w, h, bpp, rate) as its own DEVMODE with DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY set. They are reordered by include/vcr_modeorder.h: 4:3 and 5:4 sizes first at each depth, then the rest; within a rank, the miniport's table order. So the 1152x864@75 entry precedes 60/70/85.
3) win32k matches the app's partial DEVMODE to one of those entries and calls DrvEnablePDEV (line 359) with it. That matching rule is XP's and is UNMEASURED on vcr-kmd. pick_mode (line 175) and pick_refresh (line 88) then take the EXACT rate if it is listed. Otherwise they take the highest listed rate BELOW the request, never above ('that is how a CRT gets driven out of range'). A request of 0 or 1 Hz ('default') gets the LOWEST listed rate at that size. An unlisted size falls back to the largest listed size within the request, then 640x480, then the smallest mode, with a WARN. vcr_timing_find (vcr_modes.c:386) applies the same 0/1 -> lowest rule for internal lookups (vcr_edid.c:130 uses it for the 640x480@60 sanity check). The chosen ModeIndex goes to IOCTL_VIDEO_SET_CURRENT_MODE (vcrmp.c:669), and vcrmp_hw.c programs that timing's own pixel clock, logging 'mode N: WxHxBPP@Hz' and the achieved milli-Hz.
4) What win32k picked is RECORDED. Every DrvEnablePDEV writes w, h, bpp and freq into the flight recorder (vcrdd.c:425, VCR_EV_DD_ENABLE_PDEV; seen in evidence/silicon/*/vcrlog.tsv as 'DrvEnablePDEV mode 163 ... 00000055' = 1280x1024x32@85). So reading the ring after a no-rate game start answers the question on .124 without running a new tool.
5) Consequence: a title that names no rate gets XP's choice among vcr-kmd's rates; one that names a listed rate gets exactly that rate; one that names an unlisted rate gets the highest listed rate below it, which is safe.
6) Glide and the ICD on .124 bypass that. MesaFX 0.1.64's fxBestRefresh (build/retro3dfx-gl src/mesa/drivers/glide/fxapi.c:406) takes FX_GLIDE_REFRESH_RATE / SSTV2_REFRESH_RATE / MESA_FX_REFRESH if set; otherwise it asks for the highest rate EnumDisplaySettings lists at W x H (85 at 4:3 sizes), snapped down to a GR_REFRESH enum. Our h5 Glide3 hwcInitVideo (glide3x/h5/minihwc/minihwc.c) maps that enum to Hz, then REPLACES it with FX_GLIDE_REFRESH if hwcGetenv finds one (line 4675). hwcGetenv (line 9547) checks the process env, then HKCU regPath, then HKLM regPath. On .124 that finds FX_GLIDE_REFRESH="75" in the leftover Services\3dfxvs\Device0\glide (read 00:38; retro-3dfx/FINDINGS.md:422). The mode is then set with IDirectDraw2::SetDisplayMode(w, h, bpp, refresh) (win_mode.c:326) and, on failure, retried at rate 0 (lines 331/352), where XP's default applies. AmigaMerlin 3.1's glide3x also carries FX_GLIDE_REFRESH; its glide2x has no refresh override and passes the app's GR_REFRESH, as does the open glide2x/h3 source. Net effect: Glide titles on .124 run at 75, not the monitor's 85, until a per-launch FX_GLIDE_REFRESH says otherwise.
7) Observed list on .124 (GAMERES 00:26): 85 is the best rate at every 4:3/5:4 size from 320x240 to 1600x1200; 72 at 720x576, 75 at 960x720, 60 at 1280x720 through 1680x1050. There is no 100 or 120 Hz entry anywhere, even though vcr_timings has them and the EDID's vmax is 160. Either the running build predates those rows, or the range in force is not the EDID's (vcrctl info mon_src).
8) Contrary data point, unresolved: NewDark's D3D9 display on .124 opened at 1280x960x32@85 (commit 89c000f). The staged cfgs do not set d3d_disp_refreshrate, although Thief2.exe carries that cvar and the strings 'Requested refresh rate %d Hz is not supported'. Either NewDark picks the desktop's rate itself, or D3D9 on XP handed win32k 85.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (a) Per-title refresh knobs fed a per-TARGET rate. It is computed once by gr_target_hz() and published identically by GAMERES and FLEETRES.
candidate_mechanisms.how: Both writers call agent/shared/gameres.h gr_target_hz(panel, list, W, H, persisted W/H/rate). With an EDID ceiling it returns the best listed rate at that exact size, with the EDID vertical maximum applied as the list is built. Without one it returns the persisted desktop's own rate, but only at a size no bigger than the desktop and only where the driver lists that exact rate; otherwise 0, meaning leave the rate alone. It is published as FR_HZW (at FR_W x FR_H), FR_HZ43, FR_HZQ2 and FR_HZQ3 (at the id Tech 2 / id Tech 3 INDEX mode), plus FR_HZSRC. The agent tokens are %HZW% %HZ43% %HZQ2% %HZQ3%. Each title passes the rate for the resolution IT runs at, and passes nothing when the value is 0. Phase 1 is implemented and green in the worktree; see fleetres_gameres_change.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: id Tech 3 r_displayRefresh (quake3, ioquake3, jasp, jamp at FR_HZW; sof2/sof2mp and WolfSP at their Q3MODE size via FR_HZQ3). Serious Engine gfx_iRefreshRate. Halo -vidmode w,h,hz. CS 1.6 -freq: sibling evidence shows the Steam-era build 4554 hw.dll CVideoMode_OpenGL adds DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY from -freq; WON hw.dll has no -freq. Thief 2 NewDark d3d_disp_refreshrate. Glide through launcher environment variables: FX_GLIDE_REFRESH for H5 Glide3 on .124, and SSTV2_REFRESH_<W>x<H> for the Voodoo 2 on .243, which needs an operator-declared ceiling there. MesaFX 0.1.64 already asks for the best enumerated rate per W x H. Values per box: .124 gets 85 at its 4:3 targets; the LCDs get 75 at the 4:3 and index sizes (SoF2/RTCW run at 1152x864) and 60 native; .195 gets 60; .243 gets 75 only at its own 1024x768.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: Lowest risk. The rate is listed at that exact size and sits under the EDID vertical cap; with no EDID it is either the desktop's own shown rate at a no-bigger size or 0 (engine default). Because both writers call the same function, a shared cfg cannot fight, and a settled box still reports '0 value(s) changed'. Failure is visible in GAMERES JSON (hz, hz_four_three, hz_q2, hz_q3, hz_src) and in FR_HZSRC. Rollout must ship the agent, the launchers and FLEETRES.EXE in one window per box; otherwise an old writer and a new one disagree briefly. It covers only engines that have a knob.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (c) refreshkeep watcher, hardened and fed the explicit per-target rate
candidate_mechanisms.how: The launcher starts agent/tools/refreshkeep.exe <FR_HZ43|FR_HZQ2|FR_HZW> <game.exe> hidden, and skips it when the rate is 0. After the game's own no-rate mode set lands, refreshkeep re-applies the same W x H x BPP with DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY (flags 0, never CDS_UPDATEREGISTRY) and exits with the game. Hardened in the worktree: it never forces on an unknown current rate (0/1 Hz; the old rule re-applied every second forever on Win9x), and it STOPS after 3 re-applies in 60 s, which marks a title that resets its device (rk_should_force, rk_budget_ok, with tests).
candidate_mechanisms.covers: OpenGL titles with no knob, on XP: GLQuake, Quake II ref_gl, SiN, SoF, WON Half-Life GL, Hexen II glh2, and UE1 OpenGLDrv (UT, Unreal, Deus Ex). MEASURED on XP with ForceWare 71.89 (.143, 2026-09-27): Quake II went from 60.0 to 100.0 fps at 100 Hz, and UT OpenGLDrv averaged 58.6 (max 72.4) against a 60 cap. Unmeasured on ATI 8.970/8.593, NVIDIA 340.52 and vcr-kmd.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: One extra monitor re-sync about 1 s after every game mode set, and again after alt-tab or vid_restart. It must NEVER run for DirectDraw/D3D exclusive titles: MS SetDisplayMode docs say another app's mode change loses the primary surface, and a device reset at no rate then ping-pongs. It must never run for Glide/3dfx titles or on Win9x. Never pass 'max': refreshlogic's max is the driver list, not EDID-capped. It is visible in refreshkeep.log, which records each re-apply and a STOPPING banner.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (e) Request-fixing shim: add the rate at the source
candidate_mechanisms.how: A game-local proxy DLL. It could be an opengl32.dll that forwards to %SystemRoot%\system32\opengl32.dll and IAT-hooks ChangeDisplaySettingsA/ExA in the process, or ddraw/d3d8/d3d9 proxies. It fills in DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY with the gr_target_hz rate for the requested W x H, and replaces SetDisplayMode(...,0) or FullScreen_RefreshRateInHz 0 with that rate.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: Every knob-less title on every API. One mode set, correct the first time, no watcher, no device loss, and the D3D/DDraw titles that (c) cannot touch.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: Not built. It adds a new binary beside 20+ exes. It collides with game-local ICDs (our MesaFX retrogl/opengl32 on .124, nGlide) and any exe self-checks. XP only; Win9x does not need it. A bug crashes the game at start. It would need its own per-call log to make failures visible.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (d2) Monitor MODES range pinning (OS-level, the RefreshForce-era trick)
candidate_mechanisms.how: For each resolution, write Mode1="<h>-<h>,<v>-<v>,+,+" under the monitor's HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Class\{4D36E96E-E325-11CE-BFC1-08002BE10318}\000N\MODES\<W>,<H>. XP's 'hide modes this monitor cannot display' pruning then leaves only the best rate at each size, so any no-rate request can land nowhere else. The AnandTech Win2K guide reports this working for D3D but not OpenGL.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: Potentially every API, including DirectDraw/D3D titles.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: Machine-wide, and takes effect only at re-enumeration or reboot. Mis-pinning the persisted desktop's own size strands the box at a fallback mode at boot. It needs pruning enabled and is unmeasured on every fleet driver. The pins must be computed from the EDID-capped best rate per size and read back, and deleting the keys reverses it. Measure first: -list before and after, on one box, with the operator present.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (b) Launcher pre-switch
candidate_mechanisms.how: FLEETRES sets W x H x BPP at the best rate with CDS_FULLSCREEN just before the game starts, hoping the game's same-mode no-rate request keeps that rate.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: Every knob-less engine, IF the OS or driver keeps the current rate for a same-mode no-rate request.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: REFUTED on XP with ForceWare 71.89 (desktop at 100 Hz, same-resolution no-rate request -> 60; refreshlogic.h, .124, 2026-08-25). The PST KB also documents it as not working on 2000/XP. Unmeasured on ATI, where DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE exists, and on vcr-kmd. It adds a re-sync, and leaves a temporary mode if the game dies before its own mode set. modetest -b is exactly the test for this; adopt it per driver only on a KEPT verdict.

candidate_mechanisms.name: (d) Vendor and OS registry overrides
candidate_mechanisms.how: ATI 3D_Refresh_Rate_Override; ATI DALRULE_APPLYPREVIOUSREFRESHRATE; NVIDIA 340.52 UseGDIRefreshRate, 60HzOverride and EnableRefreshRateOverrideDevices; DirectDraw ForceRefreshRate (the dxdiag override: DWORD HKLM\Software\Microsoft\DirectDraw\ForceRefreshRate, 40-120); the 3dfx Glide registry values FX_GLIDE_REFRESH and SSTV2_*.
candidate_mechanisms.covers: DirectDraw apps system-wide (ForceRefreshRate), or per vendor if the undocumented switches do what their names say.
candidate_mechanisms.risks: ATI's override is vestigial: no reader in the 13.4 or 10.2 binaries. The ATI DAL rule and the NVIDIA switches are undocumented, need a reboot and are unmeasured. ForceRefreshRate is ONE rate for every mode and every DirectDraw app (Wine's clone overrides even a rate the app asks for itself), which is wrong on the LCDs whose 1080p is 60-only unless it is set and cleared around each launch, and its D3D8/9 coverage is unknown. The 3dfx registry values are 3dfx driver settings and are never changed automatically; the per-launch environment in (a) is the sanctioned route.

measurement_tool:
SOURCE (uncommitted, worktree /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/worktrees/refresh-mech, branch worktree-refresh-mech off origin/master e02dc77):
- tools/modetest/modetest.c: the Win32 tool.
- tools/modetest/modetest_logic.h: every pre-switch safety decision plus the vblank maths, with no windows.h.

WHAT IT DOES (log appended to modetest.log beside the exe and mirrored to stdout):
- Records OS, live mode (ENUM_CURRENT), persisted mode (ENUM_REGISTRY), EDID vmax/hmax/name, and every EnumDisplaySettings entry with its rate, sentinels included.
- -a: ChangeDisplaySettings(W,H,BPP with no rate, CDS_FULLSCREEN). -nobpp sends W and H only, as Quake II does.
- -b <hz|max>: CDS at <hz>, then the no-rate request, with a KEPT / DID NOT KEEP verdict.
- -c: DirectDraw exclusive SetDisplayMode(W,H,BPP,0). -cb <hz>: a CDS pre-switch, then DirectDraw rate 0.
- -d: Direct3D 9 fullscreen with FullScreen_RefreshRateInHz 0; also logs what D3D9 lists and what the device reports.
- -list: switches nothing and times the desktop.
- -restore: paced recovery; a no-op if the screen is already persisted.
- -dry: checks the requests and prints the plan.
- After every switch it reads back: eds_hz (EnumDisplaySettings), caps_hz (GetDeviceCaps VREFRESH), dd_freq (GetMonitorFrequency) and the MEASURED scanout (WaitForVerticalBlank + QueryPerformanceCounter; median interval; refused if less than 70% of samples fall within 3%). It writes one RESULT line per observation, and '!!!' when the driver's reported rate disagrees with the scanout. The measurement matters because Win9x reports 0.
SAFETY (enforced before the first switch; exit 2 if refused, nothing switched):
- Only modes EnumDisplaySettings lists, at that depth, and never bigger than the persisted desktop.
- Explicit rates must be listed, real (50-199) and under the EDID vmax and an estimated EDID hmax (h*hz*1.06). 'max' is refused when there is no ceiling (no EDID and no -maxhz).
- Refused when the live mode is not the persisted mode (Win9x 0 Hz counts as unknown, not different), on Windows 8 or later, or when the plan exceeds 12 switches.
- Every switch goes through voodoo-cleanroom/vcr-kmd/tools/vcr_pace.h, the fleet's one mode-switch gate (C:\vcr\lastswitch.dat plus the named mutex vcr-pace, shared with vcrctl), with its own floor of 5 s or more.
- Every test restores the persisted mode and READS IT BACK. A failure prints a banner and exits 3. When the pace gate refuses the give-back, the tool ends rather than give it back unpaced.
- A watchdog enforces the run budget. Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 refused, 3 restore failed, 4 a test's own mode change failed, 5 watchdog.
EXACT PLAN (tools/modetest/run_modetest.py plan; 49 switches if every step runs). Rules for every step: run one step at a time with --approved-by, and only after that screen's owner has released it. Steps with switches add '-pace 6 -hold 4' (8 on the CRTs) and a '-tag <id>' so the runner finds its own run in the appended log.

PHASE 1 (implemented):
(1) agent/shared/gameres.h (Win32-free):
- gr_mode_t gains nr + r[GR_MODE_RATES=12]: every REAL rate the size was listed at, recorded after the insert-time EDID cap (gr_mode_note_rate). gr_has_rate() reads it.
- GR_HZSRC_NONE/EDID/PERSISTED, and gr_have_ceiling(p) = p->ok && p->vmax > 0. An EDID without a range descriptor counts as no ceiling.
- gr_target_hz(p, l, w, h, reg_w, reg_h, reg_hz, &src): with a ceiling it returns gr_best_hz(l, w, h). Without one it returns reg_hz IF reg_hz is real AND w <= reg_w AND h <= reg_h AND gr_has_rate(l, w, h, reg_hz). Otherwise 0, meaning leave the rate alone, never 60. This no-EDID rule never claims the driver's unclamped best (a .133-shaped fixture: the card lists 100, the tube is shown 85 -> 85). It also keeps what FR_HZ already gives a tube at its own desktop mode (.143's 100 Hz at 1024x768), so no-EDID CRTs do not regress to XP's 60.
